s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic and laboratory evidence of myocardial injury, complicated by hypotension
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain with increasing intensity
ECG findings of ST-segment elevation and depression
Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery on emergency angiography
key_facts: Patient is an older woman
History of diabetes
History of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
Presented with sudden-onset chest pain
Initial normal heart rate and blood pressure
Later fell to 60/40 mm Hg without arrhythmia or bleeding
ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
ECG showed subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9
ECG showed downward-sloping ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4
High-sensitive troponin T level was 0.309 ng/mL
Emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
Computer tomography angiography revealed contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: ECG showed ST-segment elevation and high-sensitive troponin T level was elevated

shortlist.label: ST-elevation myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, and emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery

shortlist.label: Cardiogenic shock
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's blood pressure fell to 60/40 mm Hg without arrhythmia or bleeding

shortlist.label: Cardiac tamponade
shortlist.why_kept: Computer tomography angiography revealed pericardial effusion

shortlist.label: Coronary artery dissection
shortlist.why_kept: Emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery, which could be related to dissection

raw.rationale: The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain, ECG findings of ST-segment elevation in multiple leads, and a high-sensitive troponin T level above the reference range, which are all indicative of an ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Additionally, emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery, further supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: While the patient did have a myocardial infarction, the specific type is better described as ST-elevation myocardial infarction due to the ECG findings.

rejected.label: Cardiogenic shock
rejected.why: The patient's low blood pressure could suggest cardiogenic shock, but it is more likely a consequence of the ST-elevation myocardial infarction rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cardiac tamponade
rejected.why: Although the patient had a pericardial effusion, there is no indication that it was causing tamponade physiology, such as equalization of diastolic pressures or significant respiratory variation in preload.

rejected.label: Coronary artery dissection
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence provided for coronary artery dissection, and the thrombotic occlusion seen on angiography is more consistent with a thrombotic event in the setting of an ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
